guides.title: Tea Tasting for Beginners: Compare Two Cups
guides.description: A practical two-cup tea tasting with measured leaves, an aroma checklist, a note-taking template and fixes for bitter or weak green tea.
sections: Set up a fair comparison

Start with two small brews rather than a table full of teas. A useful first pairing is Nevisan Organic Green Tea and Spearmint Green Tea: one introduces the unflavoured leaf, the other adds a clear mint note. If you prefer to compare processing styles, use Organic Green Tea and GABA Oolong instead.

Set out two matching cups, a roomy strainer, a timer and a scale. Measure the same water volume for each cup and write it down. Use each pouch’s leaf quantity, temperature and steep time; a fair comparison does not require ignoring different preparation instructions. Label the cups before brewing so you can connect each note to the right tea.
Notice aroma, taste and finish separately

1. Dry leaf: smell the leaves before adding water. Choose an ordinary word such as grassy, minty, floral or toasty.
  2. Brewed aroma: smell the strained tea once it is comfortable to approach. Does the aroma match the dry leaf?
  3. First sip: let the tea cool enough to drink comfortably. Notice whether the flavour feels light, rounded, brisk or warming.
  4. Finish: pause before the next sip. Record what remains: mint freshness, a drying sensation, a floral note or very little aftertaste.

A flavour description is a personal reference, not a quality score. A honey-like note does not mean honey is an ingredient. Read the ingredient declaration separately.
Use a tasting note you can repeat

Copy this into your notebook:
Tea and date opened: ___
Leaf weight / water volume: ___
Water temperature / steep time: ___
Aroma / first sip / finish: ___
One change for next time: ___

For a second round, change one variable. If a cup feels too drying, shorten the next steep while keeping the leaf and water unchanged. If it is weak, first check your measurements and that the leaves had room to open. Do not add more leaf and more time together: you will lose track of which adjustment helped.
Choose the cup you want again

Try both teas plain before adding milk, lemon or sweetener. Additions change the comparison, so note them if you use them later. You do not have to finish every sample, and there is no need to turn tasting into a daily target. Both green tea and oolong contain caffeine.

Keep the note that helps you brew a cup you enjoy. On another day, repeat the same preparation before deciding that a different pack or tea type is better. Our ten-tea comparison is useful for choosing the next pairing.

guides.title: How to Buy Green Tea in India: A Pack Checklist
guides.description: Check green-tea ingredients, net weight, price per gram, manufacturer, dates and seller details, with a worked Nevisan 50g example.
sections: Start with the declaration, not the word premium

When buying green tea online, look for a readable ingredient line and an identifiable seller. A name such as pure, detox or premium cannot tell you the contents, leaf weight or preparation. A plain tea, a botanical blend and a flavoured tea are different choices; none should be confused with the others.

For example, Nevisan Organic Green Tea lists whole-leaf green tea alone. Ginger Green Tea lists green tea, dried ginger flakes and natural ginger flavour. Rum Green Tea lists green tea and natural rum flavour. The flavour declaration matters if you want a tea without added flavouring; a tasting note alone is not an ingredient list.
Compare the same quantity

Nevisan’s direct-site MRP is ₹499 for a 50g packet. That is ₹9.98 per gram. At 2–2.5g of dry leaf per first brew, a packet provides approximately 20–25 measured portions, or ₹19.96–₹24.95 of tea per portion. This calculation excludes additions and assumes one portion of dry leaf per brew; it does not promise a fixed cup size or repeat steep.

Use the same calculation when comparing a 25g pouch with a 100g pack. Check whether a listing price is for one pouch or a bundle and whether shipping is included. Our website uses free shipping, with international delivery arrangements confirmed before payment. Marketplace prices and fulfilment terms may differ.
Check five things before paying

• Ingredients: tea alone, botanicals, flavouring and any declared allergens.
  • Pack information: net weight, batch details, packed or manufactured date and best-before declaration.
  • Responsible business: manufacturer and marketer names, address and the applicable FSSAI details.
  • Evidence: ask for the relevant certification when an organic claim is important to your purchase. A logo or adjective is not a substitute for documentation.
  • Order terms: seller, delivery coverage, payment method and support for a damaged or incorrect item.

At Nevisan, GABA Oolong is manufactured by GABA TEA PVT. LTD.; the other nine teas are manufactured by Tailor Made Tea. Mahabir Enterprise markets the collection. Current business and manufacturer details are available before you order.
When the packet arrives

Check that the variety, weight and declarations match your order and that the seal is intact. Follow the physical pouch where its batch-specific information differs from an online description. Contact the seller with the order reference and clear photographs if a packet is wrong or damaged; do not rely on a review section to resolve the order.

Then brew a measured first cup using the pouch guide. Colour, bitterness or floating leaves alone cannot authenticate a tea. If something seems wrong, keep the packaging and ask the business rather than attempting a home purity test.

guides.title: Spearmint Tea and PCOS: Know What Is in Your Cup
guides.description: Understand the difference between spearmint herbal tea and Nevisan’s caffeinated green-tea blend, the limits of research and how to brew for taste.
sections: Spearmint herbal tea and this blend are different

If you arrived here looking for a PCOS tea routine, first check the ingredients. Nevisan Spearmint Green Tea combines green tea with spearmint leaves. It contains caffeine and is not a pure spearmint herbal infusion. A study of a different preparation cannot establish a result, dose or treatment schedule for this blend.

This page explains that distinction and gives a way to prepare the drink for taste. Nevisan is a tea brand; this guide is not a clinical recommendation or a hormone-treatment programme.
What the small trial can and cannot tell you

A 2010 randomized trial enrolled 42 participants for 30 days and compared spearmint herbal tea with a placebo tea. It reported changes in hormone measurements but no statistically significant improvement in the objective hair-growth rating between groups during the study. That short trial did not test Nevisan’s green-tea blend.

It does not justify promising reduced facial hair, restored fertility or a PCOS cure from a retail tea. The WHO’s PCOS fact sheet describes a condition that needs individual assessment and care. Do not replace prescribed treatment with tea or use a brand’s brewing guide as medical dosing advice.
Build a tea break around taste

If this caffeinated blend suits you, choose a time when you would normally enjoy tea. Set out a cup, a strainer with room for the leaves and a timer. Use the preparation below and remove the leaves at the end, rather than leaving them in the cup through a long meeting.

Try the first cup without sweetener so you can notice the mint and the green-tea finish separately. For the next cup, change only steep time if it is too brisk. There is no required daily number of cups, no benefit countdown and no need to drink a flavour you dislike.
Questions to take to your clinician

• Does my caffeine intake fit my circumstances and medicines?
  • Am I choosing a drink for enjoyment, or expecting it to treat a symptom?
  • Are symptoms such as changing periods or new hair growth something I should have assessed?

If you need to avoid caffeine, this green-tea blend does not meet that requirement. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, medicines and personal sensitivity are reasons to ask a qualified professional about your own situation. Product questions can go to Nevisan support; medical questions belong with your healthcare team.

guides.title: Green Tea for Energy, Sleep or Weight Loss? Choose Carefully
guides.description: Separate green-tea flavour choices from weight-loss and sleep promises. Compare caffeinated Nevisan blends and plan a practical first brew.
sections: A tea name is not a health outcome

There is no Nevisan blend we can identify as the best treatment for weight loss, low energy or sleep. Those are different needs, and our packets do not come with clinical evidence establishing those outcomes. Choose among our teas by ingredients, flavour and preparation instead of expecting a name such as chamomile or GABA to promise an effect.

The NCCIH green-tea overview describes limits in the evidence for many promoted uses. Research on an extract or a general category is not proof of a result from a particular cup. A stronger brew is not a way to turn tea into a treatment.
For a morning or work break

Start with a flavour you already enjoy. Organic Green Tea is the unflavoured option; Spearmint adds mint; Ginger has a warming note. GABA Oolong is a different tea type with a toastier profile. All contain caffeine, and we do not have a product-specific caffeine measurement to rank them from strongest to weakest.

A useful first choice is one packet, a strainer and a preparation you can repeat. Measure the leaves and use a timer. If you are buying tea to replace another drink, compare the whole routine, including sugar, syrups and portion sizes, rather than assuming every green-tea drink is the same.
For an evening cup, check caffeine first

Nevisan Chamomile Green Tea contains both chamomile flowers and green tea. It is not a caffeine-free chamomile infusion. The same distinction applies to our mint, tulsi and lemongrass blends: adding a botanical does not remove the green-tea base.

The FDA’s caffeine guidance explains that sensitivity varies and caffeine can affect sleep. If avoiding caffeine is important to your evening routine, none of our current ten teas is presented as caffeine-free. Do not choose a floral name as a substitute for checking ingredients.
Make the first packet useful

1. Pick the flavour family you like, using our comparison of all ten teas.
  2. Check the full ingredients, especially if you avoid added flavours or particular botanicals.
  3. Follow the pouch guide and taste the first cup plain.
  4. Record the time of day and preparation you enjoyed, without treating changes in symptoms as evidence that the tea caused them.

Each direct-site packet is 50g at ₹499 MRP. You can discuss any personalised offer with Nevisan on WhatsApp before paying. No health goal requires buying a bundle or committing to a daily tea schedule.

guides.title: Cold Brew or Iced Green Tea? Start with the Pack Guide
guides.description: Learn the difference between cold infusion and chilled hot-brewed tea, how to check cold-brew suitability and how to avoid a watery iced cup.
sections: Cold brew describes the preparation, not the serving temperature

Cold-brew tea is infused in cold water. Iced tea can be brewed hot, strained and then served cold. These methods are not interchangeable instructions for every loose-leaf product. Nevisan’s current product guidance gives hot-water preparation; it does not establish a tested cold-infusion time or refrigerated shelf life.

For a Nevisan cup served cold, start with the pouch’s hot-brew method and chill the strained drink promptly. Do not copy an overnight cold-water recipe onto a blend whose manufacturer has not confirmed that use.
Why cold-brew suitability matters

CVUA Karlsruhe’s food-safety explanation of cold-brew tea notes that cold water does not kill microorganisms that may be present. Refrigeration is not a substitute for product-specific preparation instructions. Tea containing dried flowers or herbs should not be assumed suitable merely because another brand sells a cold-infusion product.

If you specifically want cold infusion, ask the manufacturer whether the exact product is intended for it, and follow its water, time, temperature and storage directions. We do not supply a universal six-to-eight-hour recommendation for the Nevisan collection.
Make a small chilled hot brew

1. Use clean equipment, potable water and a heat-safe brewing vessel. Keep the dry pouch away from splashes.
  2. Measure one portion of tea and record the water volume you normally enjoy. Use the pouch’s temperature and steep time.
  3. Strain all leaves into a clean heat-safe container. Do not keep steeping while the drink cools.
  4. Chill promptly; do not leave a large warm jug standing on the counter. Make a small batch for the occasion rather than preparing days of drinks.
  5. Serve with clean ice made from drinking water. Add citrus only after tasting the plain tea.

This is a serving suggestion using the published hot-brew directions, not a validated preservation process. Follow any stricter storage or preparation instructions on your physical packet.
Fix dilution without oversteeping

Ice adds water as it melts. If your first glass tastes weak, use less ice or adjust the amount of water next time while noting the change. Increasing the steep time far beyond the pouch guide can make the tea brisker rather than solving dilution.

For a direct comparison, split one strained brew into two clean cups: taste one warm and chill the other. Note differences in aroma and strength without assuming a colder cup contains a particular amount less caffeine. Our lemongrass iced-tea recipe applies the same method to a citrus-style blend.

guides.title: Assam Whole-Leaf Tea: Green Tea, Oolong and Your First Brew
guides.description: Understand Assam origin, whole-leaf format and green versus oolong processing, then compare two Nevisan teas with their pouch brewing guides.
sections: Read origin, type and leaf format separately

Assam identifies where a tea comes from; it does not by itself tell you whether the cup is green, black or oolong. Whole-leaf describes the leaf format, while a name such as spearmint describes an added ingredient. Reading those details separately makes it easier to understand what is in a packet.

Nevisan’s collection includes Assam green-tea blends and a GABA Oolong. The oolong is not a green tea with a different flavour added. If you want to understand the base leaf before choosing a botanical blend, compare our Organic Green Tea and GABA Oolong as two separate preparations.
Green tea and oolong: a useful comparison

Green and oolong teas come from Camellia sinensis, but processing differs. The NCCIH background on tea distinguishes green tea from partially oxidized oolong. Origin alone cannot establish the finished flavour or the caffeine content of your cup.

Our catalog describes Organic Green Tea as fresh and grassy, and GABA Oolong as toasty with stone-fruit and honey-like notes. These are tasting descriptions, not added ingredients or a guarantee that every drinker will use the same words. Both products contain tea leaf and caffeine.
Give the leaves enough room

Use a basket strainer or a teapot with space for the wet leaves to move. A tightly filled infuser can make a measured portion difficult to brew evenly. Set the strainer in a heat-safe cup, weigh the dry tea and use a timer rather than judging only by colour.

Begin with 2–2.5g of leaves per cup and 85–90°C water as stated in our catalog. Organic Green Tea uses 1.5–2 minutes; GABA Oolong uses 2 minutes. The physical pouch takes precedence. Strain completely, then taste once comfortable to drink. Keep the water volume in your notes because cup sizes differ.
What whole-leaf does not establish

Leaf size alone does not prove organic certification, a health benefit, a caffeine level or how many repeat steeps a tea will provide. A leaf opening in water is useful to observe, but is not a home authenticity test. Check sourcing and certification documents separately when those details matter to your purchase.

GABA Oolong is manufactured by GABA TEA PVT. LTD.; Nevisan’s other nine teas are manufactured by Tailor Made Tea. The marketer is Mahabir Enterprise. These are distinct roles, shown with further details on our business information page.
Keep the next cup comparable

Seal the dry pouch after measuring, use a dry spoon and store away from moisture, heat and strong smells. Follow its best-before and storage declarations. If the next cup tastes different, first compare your leaf weight, water volume and steep time before concluding the tea changed.

For a botanical option after this comparison, choose one familiar note: mint in Spearmint, citrus in Lemongrass or ginger warmth in Ginger Green Tea. Our collection comparison shows the full ingredients rather than asking you to choose from a flavour name alone.

guides.title: Green Tea: Benefits Claims, Caffeine and Ingredients
guides.description: Read green-tea health claims carefully, distinguish brewed tea from extracts, check caffeine and ingredients, and prepare a measured first cup.
sections: A brewed cup is not an extract study

Green tea is a drink made from tea leaves. Concentrated extracts, capsules and topical medicines are different preparations. A result from one should not be presented as proof that a retail pouch treats a condition. Nevisan does not publish product-specific clinical results for its ten teas.

The NCCIH overview reports uncertainty for many promoted uses, and distinguishes beverage use from extracts and their safety concerns. We therefore do not sell a cup as a detox, a treatment or a guaranteed weight-loss result. Choose the flavour you enjoy and use healthcare advice for health decisions.
Read the whole ingredient list

A plain green tea contains tea leaf; a green-tea blend may also contain flowers, herbs, spices or flavouring. Nevisan Organic Green Tea is unflavoured. Blue Flower adds butterfly pea flowers; Chamomile adds chamomile flowers; Ginger includes dried ginger and natural ginger flavour. These distinctions affect the choice even when the packets share a green-tea base.

Aroma words are separate from ingredients. Honey-like, apple-like or stone-fruit notes do not mean those foods have been added. Use the product declaration to identify ingredients and ask about anything unclear before ordering. The physical packet is the reference for its batch.
Caffeine belongs in the decision

All ten current Nevisan teas contain a green-tea or oolong base and caffeine. Chamomile Green Tea is not the same as a caffeine-free pure chamomile infusion. Nor does mint, blue colour or a short steep establish that a drink is caffeine-free.

The FDA explains that caffeine amounts and individual sensitivity vary. We have not measured the caffeine in a prepared Nevisan cup, so a general tea-table number is not our product specification. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, taking medicines or limiting caffeine for a condition, ask your healthcare professional about your circumstances.
Prepare one cup you can assess

1. Read the pouch and use a clean cup, drinking water and a strainer.
  2. Measure the leaf and record the water volume. Our catalog starts at 2–2.5g per cup and 85–90°C; use the specific product’s time.
  3. Strain at the end of the steep. Taste it plain once it is comfortable to drink.
  4. If you want a lighter cup, adjust a single preparation setting next time rather than brewing longer in pursuit of a health effect.

Our brewing guide covers preparation; our ten-tea table covers ingredients and flavour. Neither is a medical dosing schedule. Keep product support and healthcare questions separate so you receive the right kind of help.

guides.title: Lemongrass Iced Green Tea: Brew Hot, Serve Chilled
guides.description: Make a small lemongrass iced tea using Nevisan’s hot-brew guide, with clear measures, chilling steps and ways to adjust ice and lime.
sections: Use the hot-brew guide for this iced tea

This is a chilled serving suggestion for Nevisan Lemongrass Green Tea, which contains green tea and dried lemongrass stalks. It is not a cold-infusion recipe. The catalog supplies hot-water directions, so this version brews hot and strains before chilling. We do not claim a tested overnight cold-brew method for this pouch.

The flavour is bright citrus with a gentle grassy finish. That makes it an option when you enjoy lemon-style aromas but want to taste the green-tea base too. Try the first glass plain before adding lime; citrus in the aroma does not mean lemon juice is already an ingredient.
Set out a small batch

• 4–5g Nevisan Lemongrass Green Tea, using the pouch’s 2–2.5g per-cup guidance for two portions.
  • 400ml potable water as a measured two-portion serving suggestion, plus clean drinking-water ice for serving.
  • A roomy strainer, timer, thermometer or temperature-controlled kettle, and a clean heat-safe vessel.
  • A small lime wedge, optional, to add after tasting.

The 400ml volume is a recipe choice, not a claim that every pouch defines a cup as 200ml. Change the batch size to the amount you plan to serve, and record the water and leaf weights together.
Brew, strain and chill

1. Heat the water to 85–90°C and pour over the measured leaves. Follow the physical pouch if its directions differ.
  2. Set a timer for 1.5–2 minutes. Keep the leaves free to open rather than compressing them in a small ball infuser.
  3. Strain completely into a clean heat-safe container. Chilling should not become extra steeping time.
  4. Chill promptly and keep refrigerated until serving; do not leave a warm jug on the kitchen counter for hours.
  5. Pour a fresh portion over ice. Taste before adding a small squeeze of lime or any sweetener.

Make a small amount for the occasion. We have not validated a storage life for homemade batches, and a clear appearance or pleasant smell does not establish safety. Use the product’s preparation and storage guidance.
Adjust the glass, not every variable

If the glass is watery, try less ice or a smaller water volume on the next batch. If it is too strong, dilute the strained tea with drinking water. If lime overwhelms the tea, leave it out and compare the plain cup first. Keep the steep time within the pouch guide before changing several settings at once.

Lemongrass Green Tea contains caffeine. Serving it cold does not make it caffeine-free, and this recipe does not establish a caffeine reduction. For the difference between cold infusion and iced tea, read our cold-brew preparation guide. The same page explains why suitability should be confirmed for the exact product.

guides.title: Which Nevisan Tea Should I Choose? A Flavour Guide
guides.description: Choose a Nevisan tea by mint, citrus, floral, warming or toasty flavour, then compare ingredients, caffeine and practical brewing needs.
sections: Choose one familiar flavour first

You do not need to know tea terminology to choose a first packet. Start with an aroma you already like: mint, citrus, ginger, flowers or a toasty cup. Then check what supplies that flavour in the ingredient list. This guide narrows the choice; the full comparison of all ten teas gives each product’s ingredients and brewing time.

If you are unsure about blends, begin with Organic Green Tea as the unflavoured reference. Comparing it with one botanical blend is more informative than buying a large selection before you know your preferences.
Match the flavour family to a first option

Fresh and grassy
Organic Green Tea has no added botanical in its declared ingredients.
Mint or citrus
Spearmint adds mint leaves; Lemongrass adds dried stalks with a citrus aroma.
Floral or herbaceous
Compare Chamomile, Blue Flower and Tulsi. They have different botanicals, rather than one shared floral flavour.
Warming or spirit-inspired
Ginger includes ginger flakes and natural ginger flavour. Rum and Whiskey use natural flavours and are described as non-alcoholic.
Toasty rather than green
GABA Oolong offers a different tea type, with toasty, stone-fruit and honey-like notes.
Fit the preparation to your day

For a desk cup, use a removable basket strainer and a timer so the leaves are not sitting in water through a call. For a shared pot, measure both the leaf and water when scaling up. If you want a cold drink, use the pouch’s hot-brew guide and chill the strained tea; do not assume all loose-leaf blends are intended for cold infusion.

A small setup is enough: a heat-safe cup, drinking water, a strainer and a way to measure a portion. You do not need a specialist tea set. The three-question tea finder is another way to narrow flavours if this is your first loose-leaf order.
Check the constraints before the name

All ten teas contain caffeine, including Chamomile and Spearmint Green Tea. None is presented as a caffeine-free evening drink. If you avoid natural flavourings, check Ginger, Rum and Whiskey carefully rather than assuming every aroma comes only from a visible botanical.

Each current direct-site tea is a 50g packet at ₹499 MRP. Begin with a quantity you can use and keep dry, following the pouch’s storage and best-before guidance. Keep a note of your first brew, then adjust one setting. Your own preference is a better guide to the next packet than a claim about detox, sleep or metabolism.

guides.title: Organic vs Other Green Tea: What to Check Before Buying
guides.description: Compare organic status separately from flavour, ingredients, freshness and price, and know which certification questions to ask a tea seller.
sections: Separate the claim from the cup

Organic status, leaf format and taste answer different questions. A tea may be sold as organic and still be a blend; a whole-leaf packet may contain added flavouring; a pleasant grassy note does not establish a farming certification. Compare each detail rather than using one word as a shortcut for the whole product.

Nevisan’s product name Organic Green Tea identifies our unflavoured option. Its ingredient declaration lists organic whole-leaf green tea. If you need certification evidence for a purchase, ask us for the applicable documentation and the products it covers. This guide does not replace a certificate or establish coverage for every tea in the collection.
Questions worth asking about certification

• Which certification or assurance scheme supports this exact claim?
  • Does the document cover the producer, processor, packer or the finished product being offered?
  • Is it current, and does its product scope match the packet?
  • Can the seller provide a readable document rather than only a logo or promotional statement?

If the answer is unclear, ask the seller before paying. Do not treat the absence of an organic label on another tea as proof that it is unsafe, or assume an FSSAI number alone answers an organic-certification question. Different declarations serve different purposes.
Compare like with like for taste

For a tasting comparison, choose two unflavoured green teas before comparing a plain tea with mint or ginger. Use the same measured water volume, separate strainers and each pack’s brewing directions. Record the leaf weight, temperature and steep time so preparation does not become an invisible difference.

Notice aroma, texture and finish. Organic status alone does not tell you which cup you will prefer, nor does a darker cup establish more nutrients or better leaf. Our two-cup tasting guide provides a simple notebook template for making the comparison repeatable.
Keep the purchase practical

Compare net weight, dates, storage guidance and seller details alongside certification. At ₹499 for 50g, Nevisan’s direct-site Organic Green Tea has an MRP of ₹9.98 per gram. Use the same unit when another listing shows a smaller pouch or a multi-packet bundle. Different marketplace offers can have different prices and terms.

When the packet arrives, check the variety and seal, then follow its batch-specific declarations. Keep the leaves dry and sealed after opening. A certification question is best resolved with documentation; a taste question is best resolved with a carefully prepared cup. You can ask Nevisan through the business contact page before choosing.
